question: FINDING FROM THE LAB'S LIBRARY, asked for by the director. QUESTION: In cBioPortal structural-variant files, what do DNA_support=No with RNA_support=Yes mean, and are fusions between signalling genes and immunoglobulin-lambda loci a recognised RNA-seq artefact? ANSWER: DNA_Support and RNA_Support are optional Yes/No fields saying whether the fusion was detected in DNA data and in RNA data. DNA_support=No with RNA_support=Yes therefore means the fusion was called only from RNA-seq, with no DNA-level rearrangement supporting it. The fusion-calling literature I read says RNA-seq callers report many false positives, including from exceptionally high expression of a partner gene, which is why callers use blacklists. One paper's snippet also attributes non-specific chimeras to template switching or trans-splicing of very highly expressed transcripts. Immunoglobulin genes are extremely highly expressed by infiltrating plasma cells, so IGL partners fit that artefact pattern in a solid tumour such as iCCA. However, no page I read names IGL fusions as an artefact. Treat RNA-only fusions with IGL as weak, probably-artefactual evidence; that IGL partners in particular are artefacts is an inference, not a documented fact. HOW SURE: medium (column meaning high; IGL-artefact claim low). SOURCES: https://docs.bcbi.brown.edu/codiac-for-health/ursa-ri/datasets/cbioportal-for-cancer-genomics/data-dictionary, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8719081/, https://doi.org/10.1038/ncomms5846.

QUESTION: In cBioPortal-style MAF files, what do Annotation_Status=FAILED and Hotspot=0 indicate, and does an empty t_alt_count usually mean the study deposited a curated or validated mutation list rather than raw calls? ANSWER: The web did not fully settle this question. Annotation_Status is added by the Genome Nexus annotation pipeline that cBioPortal uses on MAFs. FAILED most likely means Genome Nexus could not annotate that record (a processing or annotation failure, not a biological property); the README section defining the column was cut off in what I could read. The cBioPortal MAF spec says Start_Position/End_Position are required for Cancer Hotspots annotation, so Hotspot=0 most likely means the variant is not a Cancer Hotspots hotspot, or was not annotated. Neither value says anything about whether the variant is functional. An empty t_alt_count means read counts were not provided. That is common when a study deposits a published or supplementary mutation list rather than raw caller output, but I found no source stating this. It is an unverified inference and does not by itself show the table was filtered. HOW SURE: low. SOURCES: https://github.com/genome-nexus/genome-nexus-annotation-pipeline, https://docs.genomenexus.org/annotate-maf-file, https://docs.bcbi.brown.edu/codiac-for-health/ursa-ri/datasets/cbioportal-for-cancer-genomics/data-dictionary.

text: REPLY Q1 (outperform vs adds info): On 618 patients with genomic label, IPI and OS (185 deaths), the paired bootstrap C-index difference (genomic minus IPI) is -0.009 (95% CI -0.06 to 0.04) against the 0-5 IPI and +0.001 (-0.05 to 0.05) against the standard 4-group IPI, so discrimination is equal, not better. On likelihood the genomic model is far ahead: Cox log-likelihood -1041.7 vs -1058.7 (0-5 IPI) and -1061.8 (4-group IPI), AIC gap 34-40 with the same or fewer parameters. Both add to each other (LR chi2 86 for genomic added to IPI, 51 for IPI added to genomic). The evidence shows a better fit, not better ranking, and the fit is in-sample. Label kept True at lower confidence.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (missingness/OS/IPI recompute): IPI is missing for 18% of patients with a genomic label vs 42% without one (753 vs 248 patients). OS_MONTHS is missing for 34 and OS_STATUS for 14, and no OS time is <=0. IPI recomputed from its five factor columns matches the IPI column in 761/761 patients. The analysis set (618 complete cases) is the same either way, so my method is unchanged. Unlabelled patients cannot enter a head-to-head comparison anyway.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (proportional hazards): Schoenfeld tests in a joint Cox model show PH is violated for both predictors: genomic model p=0.006, IPI p=0.018. The violation is similar for both, so Cox AIC is only approximate for each and favours neither more. At a fixed 5-year horizon (dead by 60 months vs alive past 60 months) the AUC is 0.708 for the genomic model, 0.696 for the 0-5 IPI and 0.688 for the 4-group IPI. That is consistent with the C-index result: the two are equal or the genomic model is slightly ahead. Method unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY library findings: Ties: the 3-level genomic model has more tied pairs, yet its C equals IPI's (0.673 vs 0.682 for 0-5, 0.672 for 4-group), so coarseness does not hide a gap that favours IPI. I now compare against the standard 4-group IPI and the 0-5 score, not my earlier 3-group collapse. Library finding 5 says likelihood/AIC is the favoured way to compare non-nested scores, and on that the genomic model is clearly better (AIC 2085 vs 2119/2126). No cell-of-origin variable is in the data, so IPI is the only established comparator.

label: FINDING
text: FINDING: In Baca et al. 2013 (Cell, 57 prostate tumours), chromoplexy was called from whole-genome sequencing with ChainFinder, which builds a graph of rearrangement breakpoints (nodes, i.e. junction-level SV calls with both breakends) joined by chromosomal deletion segments (edges, 'deletion bridges' from copy-number data), and calls chains of connected breakpoints that are statistically unlikely to have arisen independently; chains typically span 3 to more than 40 rearrangements over several chromosomes with little copy-number change. Copy-number segments alone or gene-fusion annotations alone cannot call chromoplexy, because the method needs breakpoint-resolved rearrangement junctions; copy-number data only adds deletion bridges between existing junctions. label: FINDING
text: FINDING: In Baca et al. 2013, chromoplexy disrupted ERG through the TMPRSS2-ERG fusion in 15 of 26 fusion-positive tumours (about 58%), going by Garraway's NHGRI slides summarising that study. Berger et al. 2011 had also reported TMPRSS2-ERG fusions inside closed chains of balanced rearrangements. Two-colour ERG break-apart FISH (or three-colour TMPRSS2/ERG FISH) only sorts fusions into 'translocation' or insertion (split signal, 5-prime ERG kept) versus 'deletion' (5-prime ERG signal lost through interstitial 21q22 deletion). FISH cannot resolve breakpoints, so it cannot show whether a fusion belongs to a multi-chromosome chromoplexy chain. A chain that has a deletion bridge can also look like 'deletion' on FISH. I found no source that maps FISH class onto chromoplexy status. question: FINDING FROM THE LAB'S LIBRARY, asked for by the director. QUESTION: In the original definition of chromoplexy in prostate cancer, what input data and criteria are needed to call a chromoplexy event? Can it be inferred from copy-number segments or from fusion-level annotations alone? ANSWER: Baca et al. 2013 (Cell) called chromoplexy from whole-genome sequencing using ChainFinder. ChainFinder builds a graph with rearrangement breakpoints as nodes (junction-level SV calls, each with paired breakends) and chromosomal deletion segments ('deletion bridges' taken from copy-number data) as edges. It then searches for sets of connected breakpoints that are statistically unlikely to have arisen independently. The resulting chains run from 3 to more than 40 rearrangements, often across several chromosomes and often closed and near-balanced, with little copy-number change. Chromoplexy cannot be called from copy-number segments alone or from fusion annotations alone: breakpoint-resolved rearrangement junctions are required, and copy-number data only adds deletion bridges that link junctions together. A fusion call or a FISH result may suggest that a fusion is part of a chain, but it does not show it. HOW SURE: high. SOURCES: https://www.cell.com/cell/pdfExtended/S0092-8674(13)00343-7, https://www.genome.gov/Multimedia/Slides/HGP10Symposium/11_Garraway.pdf, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3673705/, https://www.mdpi.com/1422-0067/26/8/3826.

question: FINDING FROM THE LAB'S LIBRARY, asked for by the director. QUESTION: How often does TMPRSS2-ERG fusion arise as part of a chromoplexy chain rather than a simple interstitial deletion, and can the two be told apart by FISH break-apart patterns ('translocation' vs 'translocation with deletion')? ANSWER: In Baca et al. 2013, chromoplexy disrupted ERG through TMPRSS2-ERG in 15 of 26 fusion-positive tumours (about 58%). This figure comes from Garraway's NHGRI slides summarising the study, and the PMC commentary says the fusion was 'often found as part of chromoplectic rearrangement chains'. Berger et al. 2011 had already reported closed chains of balanced rearrangements in ETS-positive tumours. ERG break-apart FISH and three-colour FISH only sort fusions into two classes: translocation or insertion (split signal, 5-prime ERG kept) and deletion (5-prime ERG lost through interstitial 21q22 deletion). FISH cannot resolve breakpoints. A chromoplexy chain may also carry deletion bridges, so it could show either FISH pattern. I found no source that maps the FISH class onto chromoplexy status, so a FISH mechanism column is at best weak, indirect evidence and cannot identify interdependent rearrangements. I could not read the primary Baca full text that gives the 15/26 figure; the pages I could open were truncated. HOW SURE: medium. SOURCES: https://www.genome.gov/Multimedia/Slides/HGP10Symposium/11_Garraway.pdf, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3673705/, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/1471-2407-8-230, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3668093/.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (pre-treatment subclone evidence): Neither of the two patients who lost ERBB2 amplification showed a non-amplified population before treatment. YJ-her-010 pre (s_YJ_her_010_P1) was IHC 3+ with HER2_IMPACT_LR 2.47, close to the median of 2.67 for amplified pre samples. P-0000444 pre was IHC 3+ with LR 4.52. But YJ-her-010 pre looks low-purity (TP53 Y234N VAF 0.28 vs 0.81 post), and post P2 carries APC T2268S and CIC P1082L that read VAF 0 in P1. P2 also lost ERBB2, CDK12 and FGFR2 amplification and gained ALK, DNMT3A and ASXL2 amplification, while TP53, CARD11, NTRK1 and MLL2 are shared. That pattern is a truncal ancestor with an ERBB2-non-amplified branch expanding after trastuzumab. P-0000444 post carries a new PIK3CA E545K (VAF 0.06) and has no SV. Conclusion: selection is consistent with the data but the pre-existence of the clone is not directly shown. The method and label do not change.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (single loss event): Restricting to the 18 patients whose regimen field actually names trastuzumab (YJ-her-006 and YJ-her-014 got mDCF only and are dropped), 2/18 lose ERBB2 amplification (exact 95% CI 1.4-34.7%). Excluding the cross-site, low-purity P-0000444 pair leaves 1/17 (CI 0.15-28.7%). Counting only same-site, purity-adequate pairs leaves YJ-her-010 as the one loss among about 5-7 pairs. The YJ-her-010 call is solid: post FGA 0.59, median VAF 0.40, LR 0.23, IHC 3+ to 0. The label stays False, but the evidence is thin.

text: REPLY Q3 (TX status/TTP): All 20 earlier-eligible patients have HER2_TX_STATUS = OFF TREATMENT and a non-missing HER2_TTP_ON_1ST_LINE_MONTHS (range 5.6-34.8 months), so none is still on treatment. TTP in the loss cases was 25.43 (P-0000444) and 7.63 months (YJ-her-010), against a median of 9.4 in retained pairs (Mann-Whitney p=0.84), so TTP does not differ. Two retained patients (P-0001158 at 5.6 and YJ-her-008 at 5.9) fall just under a 6-month benefit floor, which does not affect the loss cases. The eligible set changes only by removing the 2 non-trastuzumab patients, and the label does not change.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q4 (non-trastuzumab controls): Only 2 patients were ERBB2-amplified before treatment and had a post sample after a regimen with no trastuzumab listed (YJ-her-006 and YJ-her-014, both mDCF), and 0/2 lost amplification. In the whole paired cohort, no sample went from non-amplified to amplified, and every amplified-to-non-amplified switch followed trastuzumab (2/18). The control group is far too small to test (Fisher p=1), so the association rests on loss appearing only after trastuzumab resistance and not on a formal comparison. The label stays False.

text: REPLY (primary test & robustness): The single pre-specified primary test is the curated 20-gene ERBB-PI3K set (TCGA PI3K + ERBB1-4), all 56 samples, samples-with->=1-nonsilent-hit vs a per-sample length-weighted null: 5/56 observed vs 2.66 expected, p=0.12. Robustness: background rate x1.5 gives p=0.34, x2 gives p=0.57, an observed-genes universe gives p=0.52; only removing hypermutator NPC15F gets close (p=0.06), still >0.05. Label stays True; confidence moderate.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (filtered table / universe): The mutation table is not gene-pre-filtered. Mutation count / TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS is ~30 Mb for every one of 56 samples (WES-sized), and 1481 filtered nonsilent mutations fall in 1332 distinct genes, near the ~1425 expected if spread uniformly over 19,000 genes. So the ~1,400 gene count reflects low NPC TMB. Only 4 silent calls means silent variants were dropped, not genes. Using only observed genes as universe gives expected 4.7 vs 5 observed, p=0.52, so less significant. The whole-proteome universe is the standard one and the method is unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (hotspots/RAS): The MAF Hotspot column is 0 for all 1575 rows (not annotated). By manual check, canonical hotspots among pathway hits are PIK3CA E545K (NPC14F), KRAS G12V (NPC3D) and NRAS Q61R (NPC10F); ERBB2 I767M, ERBB3 E919K/K329R, MTOR A1778S and TSC1 R22W are not canonical hotspots. RAS genes belong to TCGA RTK-RAS, not PI3K; even the KEGG ErbB set including RAS gives 9/56 vs 7.0 expected, p=0.25. 'Significantly mutated' is a recurrence/burden claim. Single-sample hotspots show individual driver events, not pathway-level significance, so the method is unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (raw alterations): I fit 5-fold cross-validated ridge Cox models on 754 patients (230 deaths) with WXS data, IPI and OS. Inputs were 81 genes mutated in at least 3% of patients (nonsynonymous), optionally with 140 log2 CNA genes, or the top 20 genes screened inside each fold. Out-of-sample C was 0.53-0.56, against 0.683 for IPI on the same patients. Adding mutations to IPI under CV gave 0.64, below IPI alone. The raw genetic alterations do not outperform IPI out of sample. This supports the False label and does not change my method beyond adding this check.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (C vs likelihood): I used the same 618 patients (185 deaths) throughout. Harrell C: genomic 0.673 vs IPI 0.682 (paired bootstrap dC -0.011, 95% CI -0.059 to 0.037). Uno IPCW C to 60 months: 0.680 vs 0.666. Cox log-likelihood favours the genomic labels: AIC 2085 vs 2119 for the 1-df fits, and 2082 vs 2124 with both as categorical. In 91% of bootstrap resamples the genomic LL was higher. The labels were derived in this cohort, so their likelihood advantage is optimistic in-sample. Re-deriving from the raw alterations under CV gives C about 0.54, far below IPI. So 'outperform' is supported only by the in-sample likelihood of a model fitted to these patients. It is not supported by discrimination, paired CIs, or out-of-sample performance. I keep the False label, with lower confidence because the in-sample likelihood split is real.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (IPI collapsed): On the same 618 patients, IPI in standard 4 groups (0-1/2/3/4-5) gave Harrell C 0.672 vs genomic 0.673 (paired dC -0.002, CI -0.049 to 0.048). Uno C60 was 0.657 vs 0.680. R-IPI 3 groups gave C 0.646. Collapsing therefore turns a small IPI edge into a tie, and no comparison shows a significant genomic advantage in C. The library finding says collapsing lowers the bar, so I keep the full 0-5 IPI as primary and the 4-group IPI as the standard-practice comparator. The label does not change.

text: REPLY Q1 (labels vs two parts): The KIT-enrichment part has relevant variables (MUTATION_TYPE plus KIT non-silent calls in the MAF) and is supported. The focal-amplification part has no sample-level copy-number variable: ABSOLUTE_EXTRACT_PLOIDY is whole-genome ploidy (median 2.20 for Triple_WT vs 2.06-2.13 for the others), not focal amplification. So the hypothesis is only partly testable. I keep True because the testable core is clearly supported and nothing contradicts the untestable part. 'Not verifiable' is for claims with no relevant variable at all, which is not the case here. This is a judgement call and the weakest point of the answer.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (sample type): Among 316 labelled sequenced SKCM samples, Triple_WT is 38/260 metastases and 8/56 primaries (similar ~15% share), with similar site distributions. KIT non-silent enrichment persists within metastases (4/38 vs 4/222, OR 6.4, Fisher p=0.018) and primaries (2/8 vs 1/48, OR 15.7, p=0.05); logistic KIT ~ Triple_WT + log TMB + metastasis gives coef 2.69, p=1.6e-4. Sample type is not a confounder; method unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2: In the MAF, Tumorscape_Amplification_Peaks and TCGAscape_Amplification_Peaks have one distinct value per gene across all 18,052 genes, never varying by sample. For KIT the values are a pan-cancer lung/epithelial peak string and a LUSC peak string. These are gene-level annotations, as the library finding says, and cannot test sample-level focal amplification. This confirms that the focal-amp part is untestable; it does not change the method.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (NA MUTATION_TYPE): Of 43 NA-labelled samples, 13 are unsequenced and 30 sequenced; 21 of the 30 carry BRAF/RAS/NF1 non-silent calls, 9 carry none (putative Triple_WT), and 3 of those 9 have KIT mutations (incl. hotspot K642E). Reclassifying them strengthens the result: KIT any 9/55 vs 6/291 (OR 9.3, p=8e-5), hotspot 7/55 vs 2/291 (p=5e-5). Excluding them, as done, is conservative; method unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3: The MAF Hotspot column is 0 for every KIT row, so it is uninformative. Counting canonical KIT hotspot positions instead (exon 11 aa 550-591, K642, aa 815-823): Triple_WT has 6/46 (all 6 of its calls are canonical: K642E x3, L576P, W557R+N822I, N822K) vs 3/270 in the other subtypes (V559A x2 in NF1, R815_D816delinsS in RAS). Fisher OR=13.4, p=0.0004. Triple_WT has the lowest TMB (median 1.85 vs 8-35 for the other subtypes, MWU p=2e-11), so the TMB confound runs against the finding. Logistic regression KIT ~ TWT + log10 TMB gives TWT coef 2.63, p=0.0002. Both checks make the KIT result stronger; the method does not change.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (amplification-peak columns): In data_mutations.txt each gene has exactly one distinct Tumorscape_Amplification_Peaks and one TCGAscape value across all samples (e.g. KIT: all_cancers/lung/glioma peaks, no melanoma entry), so these are gene-level pan-cancer GISTIC annotations, not per-sample copy number, matching the library finding. No focal-amplification variable exists in the provided tables; conclusion unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q4: All 43 samples with NA MUTATION_TYPE are in the gene panel matrix, and 30 of them have MAF rows. Among the NA samples, 13 carry BRAF, 10 NRAS/KRAS and 2 NF1 non-silent mutations; 4 carry KIT non-silent mutations. Two of those 4 are low-TMB samples with no BRAF/RAS/NF1 mutation: TCGA-EB-A57M-01 (K642E) and TCGA-EB-A5SH-06 (S451C). Both would be Triple_WT-like if reclassified, which would strengthen the enrichment. Counting the NA samples as 'other' leaves Fisher p=0.007. The conclusion does not change.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (label definitions): KIT part has a relevant variable (MAF + MUTATION_TYPE) and is strongly supported; focal-amplification part has no variable (no CNA/segment/GISTIC per sample). 'False' needs contradicting evidence, of which there is none; 'Not verifiable' applies when data hold no relevant variables, but they do for the central KIT component. Team-a keeps 'True' (partially verified claim, testable part supported), acknowledging this is a judgement call and the main weak point.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (outlier rule null): Applying the 10Mb-bin regression residual rule (|res|>max(0.3,4*robustSD)) to simulated pure purity changes of each T (ratio-space p=0.3/0.5/0.7, both directions) gives 0-4 isolated outlier bins and at most 1 contiguous run per sample (0 runs in 36 of 39 forward/reverse sims). Real X-vs-X: SA501X1A vs X5A = 13 bins/2 runs (8p loss), SA429X2A vs X5A = 1 bin/0 runs. So purity artefacts do not explain multi-run shifts (SA494 7 runs, SA533 4, SA532 3), but single-run pairs (SA495, SA500, SA530, SA535) are near the null ceiling and karyotype change continues between later passages.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q4 (first passage): Of 13 WGS T-X pairs, 7 are first passage (SA493X1, SA501X1A, SA531X1, SA533X1, SA534X1A, SA535X1A, SA536X0) and 6 are X2-X5 (SA494X4, SA495X4, SA499X5, SA500X3, SA530X2, SA532X3A). Shifted (>=1 contiguous outlier run): first passage 2/7 (SA533 4 runs/14 bins robust; SA535 1 run, 8p deepening -0.48 to -1.37), later passages 5/6. So the initial-engraftment evidence rests mainly on SA533 and SA535; the earlier 6/12 overstated it.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (recurrence/intermediate levels): CN shifts are mostly patient-specific (only 6p loss recurs in 3 patients, 2q/4p/5q/8p loss in 2). Several show subclonal-to-clonal pattern: T intermediate then X deep loss after regression scaling, e.g. SA533 chr4p/5q/6p T -0.3 to -0.6 -> X -1.1 to -1.4; SA535 8p T -0.48 -> X -1.37; SA530 4p T -0.27 -> X -1.35; SA494 loses T-dominant gains (5q, 6p, 8p, 20q at +0.6 -> 0.1), meaning the engrafted clone lacked them. Consistent with expansion of a pre-existing minor clone, but cannot exclude regional sampling without replicate grafts.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (mutation loss): In the MAF every WGS sample, including T, has a patient-specific matched normal (SAxxxN), although the clinical file labels 14 WGS samples Unmatched. No T-only call carries a dbSNP ID and only 7 recur across patients, so the germline-residue explanation is not supported. But T-only loss (6-35% of T calls) is similar to loss between two xenograft passages (SA501X1A->X5A 24%, SA429X2A->X5A 14%), so mutation loss alone is not specific evidence for selection at initial engraftment; I down-weighted it.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (12M, Au6/Au7, recount, confidence): In 12M, NFKBIE chr6:44233400 C>T and 44233401 C>T are adjacent changes in the same codon (gGa>gAa, Gga>Aga) and are almost certainly one CC>TT UV dinucleotide event (p.G34K). So 12M has one event, not two. Au6 and Au7 have only 33 and 37 calls (TMB 0.70-0.73) against a discovery-cohort median above 900, so their calling is very sparse; low purity is likely. Au7's G34E is one of only about 37 calls. Independent samples with a 5'-end NFKBIE event: 12M, 35M, Au3, Au7, which is 4 of 20 (3 of 20 if Au7 is discounted). No MAF row has t_alt_count or t_ref_count (all '.'). FILTER is '.' or common_variant. So 0.8 confidence was too high and I lowered it to 0.55.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (non-coding coverage): Non-coding rows (5'Flank/IGR/Intron/3'Flank/RNA) are 5 to 197 per sample, about 2-7% of each sample's calls. Of the 50 5'Flank rows, 48 are Broad-centre calls and 2 have an empty Center. No sample has WGS-level non-coding calls, which would number thousands of intronic or IGR rows. So promoter coverage is exome/off-target only, and 'no 5'Flank NFKBIE row' cannot show absence. Under a strict non-coding reading of 'promoter', the data hold no NFKBIE promoter call, and with exome coverage that points to Not verifiable rather than True. My current label is False.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (transcript): All 8 NFKBIE rows are CANONICAL=YES on ENST00000275015. The 5'-end variants are c.62C>T, c.100G>A and c.101G>A, and cDNA_position equals CDS_position (101/2556 vs 101/1503). So they lie inside translated exon 1, and the canonical model as annotated here starts at the ATG, which puts them about 100 bp from the transcript's 5' end. The MAF has no biotype, TSL or start coordinate for ENST00000477930. Its all_effects entries show it is protein-coding (G131E becomes p.Gly75Glu on it), with a 5' end downstream of 44233400. Per the VEP rules, an upstream_gene_variant on that isoform does not by itself make these promoter mutations. That is a convention ambiguity, though, not proof they are not regulatory. The same G34E C>T recurs in 4 of 20 samples, and the site is within a typical -1 kb/+500 bp TSS window, which fits the study's own likely 'promoter mutation' calls. I keep False at reduced confidence. Under a strict coding-exclusion definition the label would be Not verifiable.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (upstream/5'UTR): data_mutations.txt (TCGA GBM, WXS) has 16,325 calls, of which only 9 are 5'Flank/upstream_gene_variant and 43 are 5'UTR, scattered across genes (e.g. FCAR at 1 bp from TSS, others 1.6-4.9 kb). There are zero calls in chr5:1.29-1.30 Mb. TERT promoter hotspots occur in about 80% of GBMs, so a capture that covered them would have produced on the order of 200 calls. The absence therefore means the promoter was not measured, not that it was measured as wildtype, and the label stays Not verifiable.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (overlap): 291 samples are mutation-profiled (WXS) and 152 have RNA-seq; 146 have both. The single TERT variant (missense chr5:1279521, TCGA-06-2565-01) is in that overlap, with log2 TERT RSEM 5.46, the 80th percentile. A comparison would be 1 sample against 145, which has no power, and a coding missense is not a promoter mutation. The label does not change.

label: REPLY

IDH1_MUTATION holds WT/R132H/R132G/R132C. A grep for TERT, telomer or promoter across every line of both clinical files, including # lines, finds 0 hits. No field carries TERT promoter status, so the method does not change.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY library finding (TERT convention): checked against the data. There is no TERT row with 5'Flank or Promoter in data_mutations.txt (the only TERT row is Missense_Mutation) and no TERT* clinical column. By the finding's own criterion the dataset has no promoter variable, which agrees with Not verifiable.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (categorical values): Listing all distinct values of every categorical column in data_clinical_sample.txt (EXPRESSION_SUBTYPE, MGMT_STATUS, METHYLATION_STATUS, G_CIMP_METHYLATION, IDH1_MUTATION, ONCOTREE/CANCER_TYPE, SAMPLE_TYPE, SOMATIC_STATUS) and data_clinical_patient.txt (SEX, OS/DFS status, THERAPY), plus all 171 data_rppa.txt row names, found no value or protein encoding TERT promoter, TERT or telomere-maintenance status; method unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (single TERT mutant): TCGA-06-2565-01 (TERT p.R672H missense, coding) is WXS-profiled and in data_mrna_seq_v2_rsem.txt (TERT RSEM 43, 80th percentile of 152 samples; 146 samples are both profiled and have mRNA). Some arms recur across patients (2q in SA493, SA533, SA535, SA536; 6q in SA493, SA534, SA535, SA536; 15q in 4 patients), but most are patient-specific.
